messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 2901234567 - spike in external tool/function invocations causing tail latency and queuing. Affected: hosted text+tool endpoints in us-west1. Auto-escalating to oncall.

ana_oncall: seeing 5xx queue backs and KV cache pressure on gpu-pools-10. Latency p95 -> 1.8s, error rate -> 4.2%. Impacting customers with heavy fncall/agent workloads.

jake_sre: confirmed. Root cause looks like sudden increase in agent orchestrations invoking external actions + large structured JSON outputs. Key hotspots: model-x-large streaming path + tool-exec queue.

ana_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) soft-quarantine high-rate tenants (free/dev plans) 2) global throttle on external tool/function invocations (50% of normal) 3) disable structured-output streaming (reduce payloads) for streaming routes until stable.

sam_platform: I can push policy change for (2) and (3). Propose a 30m window then reassess. Anyone object?

arjun_oncall: +1. Also add header-based bypass for enterprise SLA customers so they keep tool access.

jake_sre: make it selective by plan and route. Example policy (apply via admin API):
```
POST /admin/traffic/policies
{
  "name": "toolcall_surge_mitigation",
  "rules": [
    {"match": {"plan": "free|dev"}, "action": {"throttle_tool_calls": "30%"}},
    {"match": {"route": "/v1/stream"}, "action": {"disable_structured_streaming": true}},
    {"match": {"header:customer_tier": "enterprise"}, "action": {"allow_tool_calls": true}}
  ],
  "ttl": "30m"
}
```

sam_platform: pushing now. curl snippet: 
```
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://admin.redwood.example/api/traffic/policies \
  -d '@policy.json'
```

ops_comms: note for comms: affected customers will see truncated tool outputs and potential errors on agent actions. Drafting short status note for workspace and support queue.

ana_oncall: executed policy push at 2901234578. Observability: reduced incoming tool-invocations by ~48% within 45s, queue depth halved. Error rate trending down.

arjun_oncall: can we also bump token quotas for enterprise to avoid throttling regressions? I can whitelist by tenant id list if needed.

jake_sre: yes whitelist applied for tenant ids in /ops/whitelist/enterprise-ids. Verify if any enterprise reported issues.

sam_platform: monitoring logs and p95 is back to ~950ms, error rate 0.9%. Keep policy active for 30m, then gradual rollback.

ana_oncall: handing off to arjun for the 30m watch window. If degradation returns, escalate to full disable of external action-exec on streaming endpoints (plan B).

arjun_oncall: on it. Will update at +15m and +30m in this thread.

incident-bot: Pager closed to oncall rotation. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/2901234567

ops_comms: customer note queued: "We performed targeted throttling of tool/function execution for lower-tier plans to protect global latency. Enterprise customers unaffected. We're monitoring and will update shortly."

arjun_oncall: +15m update: metrics stable, no enterprise hits. Keeping mitigation.

arjun_oncall: +30m update: steady. Planning staged rollback: 1) re-enable structured streaming for non-high-rate routes 2) relax tool-call throttle to 80% for free/dev then remove after hour if stable.

jake_sre: rollback steps approved. Reminder: keep the policy artifact TTL to 15m during rollback so we can reapply quickly if needed.

ana_oncall: closing actions: create post-incident ticket with timeline, root-cause hypotheses (sudden agent fanout + missing per-tenant rate limits), and follow-ups: per-tenant adaptive quotas, better observability on fncall tail latency, and automated enterprise bypass tests.

incident-bot: Incident 2901234567 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
